Subject: POC readiness — quick alignment on environment steps

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — MedSys engineering is ready to move to the hands-on POC. Before we kick off, we want a single checklist that lists who does what and the timeline so we can coordinate with our cloud team. High-level asks from our side:

- API keys and scoped service account that your runtime expects (least privilege)
- Org-level setup instructions (how to map projects/teams)
- IP allowlist entries and CIDR ranges for test traffic
- VPC peering details and contact window for peering cutover

Can your team produce a short MAP with owners and target close dates? We aim to have the environment provisioned and smoke-tested by July 10 so our stakeholders can see a working integration next week.

Sam

Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC readiness — quick alignment on environment steps

Sam — thanks. I drafted a compact MAP (attached) that breaks down responsibilities and target dates. Key points up front:

1) API keys & service account
   - Redwood action: create API key templates and a managed service principal mapping guide.
   - MedSys action: provision a service account with the following IAM roles: compute.viewer, network.viewer, and a bucket-reader role (we'll provide minimal perms).
   - Target: keys exchanged by 2026-07-03 17:00 PT.

2) Org setup and onboarding
   - Redwood: provide org onboarding doc + example config for team mapping and rate limits.
   - MedSys: confirm the project namespace to use for POC.
   - Target: org mapping confirmed by 2026-07-04 EOD.

3) IP allowlist & firewall rules
   - Redwood to provide exact egress IPs and short-lived test ports.
   - MedSys to add allowlist and confirm connectivity test window.
   - Target: allowlist in place by 2026-07-06 12:00 PT.

4) VPC peering
   - Tech lead (Priyom) to run through peering config and share the handshake steps; we prefer to do peering during a 2-hour maintenance window.
   - Proposed window: 2026-07-07 02:00–04:00 PT (low traffic).

5) Acceptance criteria & smoke tests
   - 5 templated calls at 99th p50 latency under agreed thresholds, example prompt set we will run live.
   - Sanity checks over embeddings and generation routes.

I've attached the MAP as a sheet with owners and a short runbook. Priyom — can you add the VPC peering checklist and CIDR expectations in a follow-up? Hannah — if you can confirm the acceptance criteria and sign-off flow, we'll finalize and share with Sam's cloud lead.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: POC readiness — VPC peering details and CIDR

Hi all — adding the technical specifics for peering and IPs. TL;DR: peering is straightforward but there are three items we need MedSys to confirm from their side before the window.

Required from MedSys before peering:
- Project ID for the peering route table
- Public AS path is not required; we'll use private routing (route exchange only inside peering)
- A /29 spare block for temporary egress NAT (we will only use for test traffic, not production)

Redwood-provided values:
- Peering endpoint name: redwood-med-mvp-peering
- Suggested test CIDRs: 10.244.12.0/28 (Redwood test subnet) — confirm there is no overlap with MedSys.
- Egress IPs for allowlist: 34.82.40.12, 34.82.40.13 (will be final once keys are provisioned).

Peering checklist (brief):
1) Exchange projected route table entries (we will supply JSON snippet).
2) Agree and schedule the 2-hour maintenance window (prefer 02:00–04:00 PT 7/7).
3) Perform handshake and run connectivity smoke tests (curl to /health and 5 tokenized requests).
4) Verify latency targets; if >20% over baseline, fallback to temporary NAT-based proxy.

Jonas — I'm copying you for tracing and to prepare the route JSON. Sam — can your cloud lead confirm the project ID and whether the suggested /28 collides? If yes, provide an alternate non-overlapping /28.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Sam — thanks for confirming the project ID and alternate CIDR. Final checklist for sign-off and close:

Owner assignments and close timeline (final):
- Soojin (Redwood): deliver MAP workbook and api-key templates — CLOSED (sheet v1 shared 7/1).
- MedSys (Sam/DevOps): confirm project ID and add allowlist entries — CLOSED (medsys-poc-2026).
- Priyom (Redwood): run peering and handoff route JSON — scheduled 2026-07-07 02:00–04:00 PT.
- Jonas (Redwood): run post-peering latency smoke tests and report — target 2026-07-07 06:00 PT.

Acceptance criteria to mark POC environment as "ready":
- All API keys successfully authenticate and return 200 on /v1/health.
- 5 templated generation calls complete with p50 latency < 250ms and p95 < 900ms for test prompts.
- Embeddings endpoint returns vectors with cosine similarity > 0.86 for the seeded sample set.

If we meet the criteria by 2026-07-07 08:00 PT, we'll move to an internal demo later that afternoon. If any item fails, we'll document the regression in the MAP sheet and propose a rollback to a NAT-proxy plan (fast fallback).

Sam — please confirm you'll add the allowlist and that your team has contact on call for the 02:00 PT window. I'll be on the call as well.

Cheers,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
